current.text: Orlando's projected starters are Suggs, Bane, Franz Wagner, Banchero and Carter. Black is expected to be the sixth man and the main creator for the bench units.
Experts call him overrated. In a 9-cat mock draft he went way too early in round 9.
He would start and be worth rostering if Jalen Suggs gets hurt.
Last season he scored 15 points per game, but after December he settled in at 12 to 13 points per game.
Yahoo lists him as questionable with an ankle injury.
He is due a new contract. Orlando is 2.5 million USD under the second apron and will likely have to choose between keeping Suggs and keeping Black.
Phil expects his new contract to be worth at least 23 million USD per year.
Orlando has a new head coach, Sean Sweeney, who replaces Jamahl Mosley. Player roles may change.

durable.text: His usage is above 20%, but he does not pass much for a ball handler. He averaged only about 3.5 to 3.7 assists last season.
He is a good on-ball defender, but screens give him trouble and he is not at Suggs's level on defense.

note: He is priced as a last-round or waiver player: Yahoo ranks him 148 at 0 USD, ESPN ranks him 128 at 1 USD, and nobody drafted him in our league last season. Steals are his only clear plus (1.4 per game, z +1.3). His FG%, FT%, rebounds and turnovers all sit a little below average, and no category is weak enough to make him a punt fit. Since the experts call him overrated as a bench sixth man, don't spend more than 1 USD on him. Early in the season, check his ankle, how many bench minutes Sweeney gives him, and whether Suggs stays healthy, because a Suggs injury makes him a waiver add.
